measure.description: The observable outcome that proves it, such as a command and its output.

spec_ref.description: Slug of the spec this plan implements.

why_this_order.description: Why this phase is here and not earlier or later.

task_criteria_map.description: Every AC id of the spec that this plan delivers. Each must be owned by a task; list the owners in task_owners.

corpus_steps.description: Document work in the corpus (convert, supersede, archive) that the plan performs.

after_landing_steps.description: What happens once the branch lands: the full suite, rebuilds, handoffs.

close_condition.description: What exactly closes the plan, including the plan's own documents and its tasks.

dimensions.question: Does any phase refuse or depend on something a later phase delivers? State the dependency chain.
Is every AC of the spec owned by a task? Name the ACs and the tasks.
What exactly closes this plan, and which of its own documents must be in which state?
Which files or claims do other sessions' plans share with this one, and how is the overlap handled?
What does the plan cost in tasks, agent runs and verification, and what is the cheapest cut that still meets the goal?
Does this change repeat one pattern across many sites? If so, which script does it and which sites need hand work? If not, say why (an na answer states the reason).
